title: Model Landscape Sentinel: prioritized probes, sourcing hypotheses, and signal contracts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a lightweight, repeatable 'sentinel' process that continuously probes emerging open and proprietary model variants for enterprise-fit signals and surface-level fallback readiness. This ticket scopes the initial probe matrix, the decision contract for promoting a model into the fallback roster, and the minimum evaluation artifacts required for procurement and Dedicated onboarding.

Why: repeated competitive disruptions (new quantized variants, region-specific forks) require a low-friction pipeline that translates surface telemetry into prioritized sourcing hypothesis and operational playbooks. Current approach is ad-hoc and gated in research; we need productized signal outputs that can be consumed by procurement, runtime, and console teams.

Deliverables:
- Probe matrix (latency buckets, embedding/LLM task coverage, quant/FP variants) with priority weights for enterprise use-cases.
- Signal contract: what telemetry + manual probes constitute 'fallback-ready' (compatibility, token-cost delta, SLO delta, license risk).
- Lightweight eval artifact template (prompt set, regression acceptance thresholds, smoke-run dashboard) to be stored in the signal-hub.
- Onboarding checklist to hand to Dedicated/Private infra (kernel affinity notes, quantization caveats, KV cache sizing guidance).

Scope decisions and trade-offs made so far:
- We will prioritize probes that exercise real customer workloads (RAG, summarization, embeddings) rather than pure bench scores. Trade-off: slower probe cadence for higher signal fidelity.
- Initial coverage will focus on models that materially change cost/latency trade-offs (sub-8B quantized variants, trimmed context-length forks). We defer exotic multimodal forks to a later phase to keep scope manageable.
- The signal contract will be intentionally conservative: a candidate must not regress on top-10 customer prompts by >5% quality (as measured by our rapid eval rubric) OR must show >=20% token-cost improvement with <10% latency regression. These thresholds are provisional and will be iterated after two weeks of pilot probes.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Tomás: finalize probe matrix CSV and upload to Confluence (ETA 2026-03-12).
- Research: run pilot probes for three candidate model variants and post smoke dashboards (ETA 2026-03-19).
- Procurement liaison (Lena Cho): draft license-risk checklist for each candidate (ETA 2026-03-22).
- Runtime (ENG): estimate kernel affinity and KV cache implications for top-2 candidates (ETA 2026-03-25).

Success metrics:
- Two fallback-ready model entries with complete signal artifacts created in the signal-hub by 2026-04-01.
- Reduction in manual evaluation time for candidates by 40% (measured vs baseline).
- A clear handoff artifact consumed by Dedicated provisioning with kernel/quant notes attached.
